confidence_notes: Low confidence: Uyuni is a small tourist town with sparse, partly generic price data. I ran six searches (one RBA, five price checks) and read only the search-result summaries. The RBA rate comes from a summary of its exchange-rates page. Beer: a nightlife guide cites about US$1.50 average, and an older blog cites 16-20 Bs for a big bottle. Cappuccino: about US$1.50-2.50. Cheap meals: 12-25 Bs. Mid-range mains: 50-80 Bs. I found no Uyuni cocktail price and no restaurant price for a glass of wine. Cocktail (about 1.7x beer) and wine glass (about 1.45x beer) are therefore relationship-based. I treated modeled aggregator figures (about US$4 coffee, about US$10 cocktail) as outliers. Guides convert at about 6.9 Bs/USD, but one source cites about 9.5 Bs/USD for April 2026. I shaded USD figures about 10% below official-rate conversions, and true values could be up to about 25% lower. Accommodation anchors are holistic estimates for July peak season, not checked against any listings.
comparable_city_reasoning: Tourist-oriented Bolivian altiplano gateway town. Priced off Bolivia-wide cost-of-living averages and La Paz/Sucre tourist-strip levels. Small premium for remoteness and July peak season, mainly on accommodation.
